question: Drug of choice for peptic ulcer disease caused by chronic use of NSAIDS:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Misoprostol" -> "increased prostaglandin production" -> "enhanced gastric mucosal protection" -> "reduced NSAID-induced gastric damage" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Esomeprazole" -> "reduced gastric acid secretion" -> "decreased gastric acidity" -> "promoted ulcer healing" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Pirenzepine" -> "reduced gastric acid secretion" -> "possible ulcer healing" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Loratadine" -> "antihistamine effect" -> "no direct effect on gastric mucosa" -> "unlikely to treat peptic ulcer" -> 20%
analysis: Peptic ulcer disease caused by chronic use of NSAIDs is often due to the inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis, which leads to decreased gastric mucosal protection. Misoprostol is a prostaglandin E1 analog that can help prevent NSAID-induced gastric ulcers by replacing the protective prostaglandins. Therefore, it is the drug of choice for this condition. Esomeprazole, a proton pump inhibitor, can also be used to reduce gastric acid secretion, but it does not address the prostaglandin deficiency directly.
